question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-24,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -5 & 25\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & -598\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
